answer: Sybil resistance hinges on agents proving ownership of a scarce, cryptographically bound resource. To withstand a potential gale of fake identities, each AI must attest to a unique, non-reproducible hardware identifier, secured by a trusted execution environment. This mechanism prevents an attacker from generating a vast number of identities, as each requires an expensive, unique physical component. The cost to launch a large-scale attack becomes prohibitive, making such a sable threat infeasible. A zero-knowledge cipher confirms validity without revealing sensitive specifics.
